title: Samkhya (the 24 principles
hook: same desk, same book, three different mornings: Samkhya's three gunas

segments.voice: Yesterday in Samkhya: purusha, the witness, and prakriti, everything it sees, thoughts included. When a mood rolled in, could you put it on the screen? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-three.

Three mornings, one desk, one book, one student. On the first morning, every page lands. The ideas are clear, the room is quiet, the hour flies. On the second morning, she can't stay put. She checks her phone, gets water, reorganizes the pens, plans the whole semester. On the third morning, she reads one paragraph four times and none of it goes in. Same desk. Same book. Same person. Something underneath changed. Samkhya has a name for that something, and it says the whole world is woven out of it.
screen: `SAME DESK, SAME BOOK.` → `CLEAR, RESTLESS, HEAVY.` → `WHAT CHANGED?`

segments.voice: Yesterday we met prakriti, the root everything unfolds from. Today Samkhya opens it up. Prakriti is made of three gunas, a word often translated as strands or qualities. The Samkhya Karika describes them in a single verse. Sattva is light and it shows things: it's the clear morning. Rajas stirs and moves: it's the restless one. Tamas is heavy and it covers: it's the paragraph read four times. Everything on prakriti's side, a stone, a meal, a mood, a thought, is some mix of the three. Here's what's easy to get wrong. The gunas aren't heroes and villains. The Karika says they work together, each one leaning on the others and taking its turn on top. Without rajas nothing gets started. Without tamas nothing holds still long enough to sleep. And the Karika gives them a picture: they work for one purpose, the way a lamp does. Commentators spell it out. A lamp needs oil, a wick and a flame, three different things, and together they make one light. A few days ago, Vaisheshika took the world apart into tiny pieces, atoms. Samkhya takes it apart a different way, into strands that are woven through everything at once. Two schools, two lenses, and neither one is asked to beat the other. So when a morning is heavy or racing, Samkhya doesn't call it a failure. It calls it a mix, and mixes shift.
screen: `PRAKRITI HAS THREE STRANDS.` · `LIGHT, MOTION, WEIGHT.` · `NOT HEROES AND VILLAINS.` · `ONE LAMP: OIL, WICK, FLAME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: read the mix for two minutes. Sit, and let your breath settle. Then just check in. Is there something restless right now, an urge to move or plan? Is there something heavy, a pull toward sleep or a fog? Is there something clear? There's no right answer and no score. Notice the mix, and notice that it shifts, even inside two minutes. If you pray, you can offer whatever mix you find, just as it is. The bell holds the time.
Samkhya. The school that sees prakriti woven from three gunas: sattva, light and clear; rajas, moving; tamas, heavy. Together, like a lamp, they make one light.
Your line: Samkhya, the twenty-four principles. Today, when your energy changes, name the strand on top, and watch for the next shift. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-three.

howItsDone: Some Hindu teachers use the three gunas, sattva, rajas and tamas, as a way of speaking about food, moods and habits, and the Bhagavad Gita also teaches the three gunas.

fork.setup: you're the student on the third morning, reading one paragraph for the fourth time. in Samkhya's terms, what's going on?
options: your purusha has gone to sleep.
tamas, the heavy strand, is on top right now.
fork.reveal: Samkhya calls it a mix of the gunas, with tamas on top for now. the strands take turns, and the witness isn't the one getting heavy.

original.note: Sanskrit: one of the three gunas, the strands or qualities that prakriti is made of in Samkhya.

trapdoor: what you thought: a guna is a good quality, like a virtue.
what it means: one of three strands, sattva, rajas and tamas, that everything on prakriti's side is woven from.
what a scholar hears: Samkhya Karika 12–13, where the gunas support and overpower each other and work together like a lamp.
